extraction.name: Leaming Multiple La y ers of F eatures from Tin y Images
extraction.description: A paper on learning multiple layers of features from tiny images
extraction.creator: Alex Krizhevsky
extraction.rai:dataCollection: Groups at MIT and NYU have collected a dataset of millions of tiny colour images from the web. The dataset was collected over the span of six months; it was assembled by searching the web for images of every non-abstract English noun in the lexical database WordNet. Several search engines were used, including Google, Flickr, and Alta vista and roughly the first 3000 results for each search term were kept.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: The dataset contains 80 million colour images downscaled to 32x32 and spread out across 79000 search terms.
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: The images were preprocessed using a ZCA whitening transformation.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: A subset of the tiny images dataset was labeled by paid students. The labeled subset consists of ten classes of objects with 6000 images in each class.
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: The dataset can be used for unsupervised training of deep generative models, object recognition experiments.
